wormholeTech.exiledSector_wormhole_bluep: Calibration routines, field geometry and fuel-feed schematics lifted from the Explorarium anchor cache in Limbo. The science teams have spent weeks tracing how the Domain held a wormhole's far end steady, and believe they can build a lattice that does the same for a single set of coordinates. Not a gate. Nothing like one. But it opens.
wormholeTech.exiledSector_gateway_upgrad: Field readings taken on the far side of a deep chart. The lattice can be retuned to hold coordinates that drift further from known space.
A full map of how the deepest charts fold. With it, the lattice can hold anything the charts can reach.

chart.anomaly.excavation_sites.dialog.op: A bored shaft cuts through the crust of {planet} into a sealed bolt-hole from the AI Wars. It is no wider than a destroyer's beam, and something in the cavern below still answers your survey drones.
chart.anomaly.excavation_sites.dialog.co: A bolt-hole from the AI Wars lies under the crust of {planet}. Its shaft caved in long ago, and only marines on foot can work through the rubble.
chart.anomaly.excavation_sites.dialog.fo: Your navigation team flags something odd in the survey sweep of {planet}: a gravimetric shadow under the crust, perfectly round, running straight down for several kilometres before stopping at a flat floor. Your navigator points out that nature rarely drills in straight lines.
chart.anomaly.excavation_sites.dialog.id: Your science team checks the shape against the fleet's archives and turns up an old Domain war record. It is a bolt-hole from the AI Wars, one of the hidden caverns dug to keep ships and stores out of reach of orbital strikes. Most were sealed and forgotten when the fighting ended. Your science officer notes, with some enthusiasm, that the record never mentions anyone coming back to empty this one.
chart.anomaly.excavation_sites.dialog.sc: Your salvage team sends a flight of drones down the shaft. It is bored clean and no wider than a destroyer's beam, and it opens into a cavern far larger than anyone expected. Halfway through the first sweep, something below locks a targeting sensor onto the lead drone. Your salvage chief recalls the flight at once and reports, a little pale, that "the place is occupied."

Your salvage team sends a flight of drones down the shaft and finds it caved in a few hundred metres below the surface. The smallest drones thread through gaps in the rubble and reach the cavern beyond, where someone has shored up the rock and posted a watch. No ship will fit through, your salvage chief reports, but a squad of marines with cutting gear could.
chart.anomaly.excavation_sites.dialog.st: In the drone footage, your salvage team picks out long racks of weapon mounts along the cavern walls, and fighter cradles with their wings still folded.

The drone footage shows a sealed archive vault near the cavern floor. Your science officer is fairly sure the data cores inside hold production patterns, and would very much like to be the one to open it.

One drone's footage shows a shielded vault with a familiar lattice of cooling lines behind its door. Your science officer goes quiet for a moment, then suggests that nobody mention the vault in any report the Hegemony might read.

The drone footage shows the cavern stacked deep with sealed supply crates, still stamped with Domain logistics codes. Your quartermaster starts working out cargo space before the footage has finished playing.
The drones pick up a faint shimmer near the cavern floor. Your science team enhances the footage and finds sealed canisters of dormant nanoswarms, still holding their charge after all this time.
The drone footage shows a bank of Nanite Feedstock tanks along the back wall, their seals unbroken. Your salvage chief remarks that whoever stocked this place expected a much longer war.

One drone's footage lingers on a rack of data cores still drawing trickle power. Your science team reads their headers as combat subroutines, written for warships that no longer exist and still waiting to be installed.
One drone's footage shows a navigation office with its wall displays still lit, plotting routes to systems that appear on no modern chart.
chart.anomaly.excavation_sites.dialog.de: Only frigates and destroyers fight, on either side. Your cruisers and capital ships hold station above the shaft.
chart.anomaly.excavation_sites.dialog.no: You have no combat-ready frigate or destroyer.
chart.anomaly.excavation_sites.dialog.cl: The bolt-hole under {planet} has been emptied.
chart.anomaly.excavation_sites.dialog.si: Nothing below answers. Whatever held the cavern is long gone.
chart.anomaly.excavation_sites.objective: Whatever the garrison sealed in below the rubble.

chart.atlas.anomaly.pre_collapse_facilit: A Domain research facility from before the Collapse, still guarded by the Remnant. Your science team would love a look at its databanks.

The defense fleet breaks orbit to intercept.

chart.atlas.anomaly.coronal_hypershunt.d: A Domain coronal hypershunt sits in the corona of a blue supergiant. It's beyond repair, but something is still guarding it.
chart.anomaly.coronal_hypershunt.intel: A coronal hypershunt orbits {star}, still guarded.
chart.anomaly.coronal_hypershunt.descrip: The hypershunt fills the sensor display long before it fills the viewports, a Domain megastructure built into the star's corona. Most of its surface is dark.
chart.anomaly.coronal_hypershunt.guarded: Several shapes detach from the superstructure and accelerate towards your fleet. Their profile matches nothing on record.
chart.anomaly.coronal_hypershunt.beyondR: Salvage crews board the structure and find its distributed repair nodes burnt out. No amount of metals or transplutonics will bring it back online.

chart.anomaly.listening_post.status.alar: The depot has raised the alarm. {value}% of its vault remains.
chart.anomaly.listening_post.status.guar: Its pickets are gathering to guard it.

The depot's vault has been taken without raising the alarm.
chart.anomaly.listening_post.dialog.desc: This {faction} depot holds a quiet orbit well clear of any traffic lanes. Behind its armor sits a stocked vault.
chart.anomaly.listening_post.dialog.quie: The depot's docking beacon is quiet, a futile attempt to hide its spoils. Your sensor XO doesn't think anyone on board has noticed you yet.
chart.anomaly.listening_post.dialog.infi: Your marine commander hand-picks a squad and a shuttle with its transponder pulled. They cross the last stretch of the dark on puffs of cold gas and latch onto the hull beside a maintenance lock.

A few quick cuts with low-EM tools with some clever rewiring and the lock cycles open with a hiss. The corridors beyond are dim and empty, at least from what you can see on the marine team's feed. Somewhere deeper in the station a work crew is arguing over a cargo manifest, loudly enough to cover the muffled sound of gravboots on deck plating.

Your squad encounters their first guard dozing at a checkpoint. They never reach the comm panel. Two more round a corner at the wrong moment and go down without a shot fired. The duty officer in the security office makes it halfway to the alarm switch, which is further than anyone else gets.
The garrison is bound, gagged and stacked in a storage locker with a ration bar each. Your techs take over the security console, every one of them reporting all quiet.

The vault door opens to the duty officer's own TriPad. Inside, under the hum of climate control, stand row after row of weapon racks, ship parts packed in shock-foam crates and a locked case of blueprint packages.
chart.anomaly.listening_post.dialog.guar: The alarm is up and the depot's garrison holds it, scuttling the vault crate by crate. {value}% of the vault remains.
chart.anomaly.listening_post.dialog.purg: The alarm is up, but nobody is left to hold the depot. {value}% of the vault survived the scuttling.
chart.anomaly.listening_post.dialog.take: The vault stands open and empty.
chart.anomaly.listening_post.dialog.stal: The depot is dark. Whatever it stored is gone.
chart.anomaly.listening_post.dialog.empt: The vault holds nothing worth taking.
chart.anomaly.listening_post.dialog.lane: The depot's supply logs chart the Outer Reach Atlas {count} lane around this system.
The depot's supply logs chart the Outer Reach Atlas {count} lanes around this system.
chart.anomaly.listening_post.dialog.opti: Take what is left of the vault
chart.atlas.anomaly.spatial_breach.descr: A tear into hyperspace. Your salvor crew thinks it's very likely to attract attention when opened, and are practically salivating at the valuable caches it could drag out of hyperspace.
chart.atlas.anomaly.faction_skirmish.des: Two factions fight over this border system. You could side with one of them or stay out - the choice is yours.
chart.atlas.anomaly.relay_network.descri: Your salvor chief notes the various dormant relays here could be a generous source of information. They also stress the importance of accessing the caches of all three, and preferably also the largest fleet in the system.

chart.anomaly.faction_skirmish.intel: Two factions are fighting over the system.
chart.anomaly.relay_network.intel: Three dormant Domain-era relays sit in the system.

{count} of the three Domain-era relays are awake.

chart.anomaly.relay_network.intel.last: All three Domain-era relays are awake. Destroy the Star Chart Boss for a unique hull item or subroutine.
chart.anomaly.relay_network.intel.traced: All three Domain-era relays are awake. Their trace leads to stage {stage} of {stages} in another Atlas system.
chart.anomaly.relay_network.nav_buoy.des: A Domain-era nav buoy, dark for centuries. Its telemetry core is intact, and the hull around its docking collar is scored by recent contact. Someone has been tethering to it.
chart.anomaly.relay_network.comm_relay.d: A Domain-era comm relay, silent but still listening for a familiar handshake. Its message buffer is not empty, which is unusual for a relay left to sit this long.
chart.anomaly.relay_network.sensor_array: A Domain-era sensor array, its dishes frozen mid-sweep. Someone has bolted a modern data tap to the housing, crudely, and left it there.
chart.anomaly.relay_network.trail.first: Your navigator points out burn scarring along its approach vector. Other crews have been here, and not long ago.
chart.anomaly.relay_network.trail.middle: Your navigator matches the burn scarring here to the logs recovered from the last network. The same crews came this way, following the same trace.
chart.anomaly.relay_network.trail.last: The trace your navigation and science crews have pieced together ends in this system. Whatever the other crews were chasing, it is here.
chart.anomaly.relay_network.log.first.na: The buoy's traffic log is mostly Domain-era survey routes. Appended in a modern format are the burn plots of three salvage crews, all from the last few cycles, all on the same heading out of the system.
chart.anomaly.relay_network.log.first.co: The buffer holds a fragment of tight-beam chatter between two salvage captains. One asks whether the other has "seen it running". The reply is a set of coordinates and a request to keep the channel closed.
chart.anomaly.relay_network.log.first.se: The array's last sweep is still in memory: an energy signature your science officer cannot match to any registered drive, reactor or weapon. The data tap was set to copy it out, and someone did.
chart.anomaly.relay_network.log.middle.n: Four crews have written over the buoy's log since the last network. Your nav team overlays their plots. They converge further out, and only two of them come back.
chart.anomaly.relay_network.log.middle.c: The buffer carries an outbound burst under three layers of encryption. Your science team strips them over two days. It is an auction notice. The lot is not described, and the reserve price is listed as "negotiable, in hulls".
chart.anomaly.relay_network.log.middle.s: The array has been retuned to watch for a single signature, the one from the last network, and it has logged it twice. Both times the source was moving, under power, and escorted.
chart.anomaly.relay_network.log.last.nav: The burn plots end here. Every crew that followed the trace reached this system, and since then the buoy has logged only one fleet holding station in it. Your navigator suspects it is not guarding the system.
chart.anomaly.relay_network.log.last.com: The buffer holds one message on a loop, broadcast in the clear: the commander of the largest fleet in the system, declining every offer. Their flagship's transponder code is attached, which reads less like an oversight than an invitation.
chart.anomaly.relay_network.log.last.sen: The tuned sweep finds the signature at once. It is not in a derelict or a cache. It is aboard the flagship of the largest fleet in the system, and it is running.
chart.anomaly.relay_network.wake.nav_buo: It wakes once your fleet holds station beside it, moving slowly, for a few hours, and its power is restored.
chart.anomaly.relay_network.wake.comm_re: It wakes once your transponder stays on in its range for a few hours, and its power is restored.
chart.anomaly.relay_network.wake.sensor_: It wakes once you fire an Active Sensor Burst in its range, and its power is restored.

chart.anomaly.relay_network.awake: It is awake and transmitting to your fleet.
chart.anomaly.relay_network.stale: The relay is dark, and nothing answers.

chart.anomaly.abyssal_shipyard.name: Abyssal Shipyard
chart.anomaly.abyssal_shipyard.descripti: Slipways hold drone hulls at every stage of assembly. Somewhere inside, fabricators are still running.

chart.anomaly.abyssal_research_complex.d: Laboratory rings turn slowly around a core that still draws power. The instruments inside are calibrated for matter that only exists in the abyss.

chart.atlas.anomaly.abyssal_storm.descri: Storms sweep through this part of the abyss. While one rages, anything outside the fog shows up on every sensor nearby.
chart.anomaly.abyssal_storm.intel: Abyssal storms flare every half minute or so. Fleets outside the fog are easy to see while one lasts.
chart.atlas.anomaly.domain_mothership.de: A Domain-era survey mothership is still following its last orders, building drones and sending them out. Your salvor chief only has eyes for the mothership.

chart.poi.abyss_research_station.name: Abyssal Research Station
chart.anomaly.derelict_forge.description: The station's spine is dark from end to end, except for a single point near its core that is very much not. Your sensor officer identifies the heat signature as an active Domain nanoforge, then checks the reading again, eyes wide. The forge's control rooms are scattered through the dead sections around it. It takes your science team some time to dig up the right ancient protocols, but each one still answers a handshake ping.
chart.anomaly.derelict_forge.guarded: As your fleet closes in, the station's Domain-era defenses power up. A Guardian and its drone escort move to intercept.
chart.anomaly.derelict_forge.guards.name: Forge Defenses
chart.anomaly.derelict_forge.runsLeft.on: It can run one more program.
chart.anomaly.derelict_forge.stock: You have <hl>{metals}</hl> metals, <hl>{rareMetals}</hl> rare metals and <hl>{feedstock}</hl> Nanite Feedstock.
chart.anomaly.derelict_forge.route.graft:
The route to the grafting controls runs through a collapsed fabrication gallery. Your salvage team spends the better part of a shift cutting through fused bulkhead plating and a curtain of dead conduit, while your science officer catalogues the junctions and asks them repeatedly "not to cut that one."

The control room behind it is intact. Its consoles show a single hull item in outline, with a bright open platform beside it waiting for something new to be joined on.
chart.anomaly.derelict_forge.route.excis:
The excision controls sit behind a stretch of corridor packed with Domain-era wreckage: shelving, crates and what may once have been a cargo drone, all compressed into one solid mass. Your salvage chief calls it "the honest kind of debris" and cuts a tunnel through it in a little under four hours.

Inside, the consoles wake to a cutting schematic. The station seems to know precisely what it intends to remove, and is only waiting to be told which part.
chart.anomaly.derelict_forge.route.perfe:
Reaching the calibration suite means crawling a maintenance shaft whose wiring has long since gone dark. Your science officer insists the teams map every dead line before anyone cuts it. Your salvage chief would like it on record that this took two hours longer than simply cutting it all.

The suite is spotless. Its displays show tolerance bands narrowed to a single line, and a measurement rig that has kept itself calibrated for two hundred cycles with nothing to measure.
chart.anomaly.derelict_forge.route.ancho:
The reconstruction controls are three decks down, past a stairwell choked with collapsed gantry and loose cable. Your salvage team cuts a path through, braces it, and cuts again when the bracing gives way. Nobody is hurt, which your salvage chief describes as "the plan working".

The control room's consoles are built around a single fixed point, with everything else on the schematic drawn as a loose, shifting shape around it.
chart.anomaly.derelict_forge.route.retem:
The tempering controls lie beside the old heat exchangers, where the air is still warm and every surface is scaled with Domain-era residue. Your salvage team cuts through a sealed hatch and a mat of fused wiring, working in short shifts.

The room beyond holds a quiet annealing rig and a console showing a slow cycle of heating and cooling, ready to be run once more.
chart.anomaly.derelict_forge.route.infus: The infusion chamber lies past laboratories still lit for experiments nobody finished. Your science officer asks the crew not to touch anything, then touches something.
chart.anomaly.derelict_forge.program.gra: Adds a modifier of a chosen ship part to an item with room for one.
chart.anomaly.derelict_forge.program.per: Sets a chosen modifier's values to the top of their range.
chart.anomaly.derelict_forge.program.anc: Rerolls every modifier except a chosen one.
chart.anomaly.derelict_forge.program.ret: Rerolls a hull item's implicit values, keeping the better roll for each.
chart.anomaly.derelict_forge.program.inf: Adds the Abyssal Rift modifier for the item's part to an item with room for it.
chart.anomaly.derelict_forge.bench.title: Derelict Forge
chart.anomaly.derelict_forge.bench.empty: Click a hull item in Hull Item Storage to load it into the forge. It stays in storage while it is loaded.
chart.anomaly.derelict_forge.bench.run.t: Runs the program on the loaded item. Its cost is taken when the program runs.
